So when I saw them being whipped[g] and made to suffer like this, I was grieved for them. They were being tormented without any relief. I asked the shepherd who was speaking with me[a], “Sir, who is this shepherd? He is so[k] pitiless and harsh and shows these sheep no mercy.”

He answered, “This is the angel of punishment[b]. He is one of the righteous angels. He is appointed to oversee punishment. So he takes charge of those[h] who have wandered away from God and followed the desires and deceptions of this age. He punishes them as they deserve with many kinds of terrible punishments.”

“Sir,” I said, “I want to know what these different punishments are.”

He replied, “Listen. These different punishments and torments are sufferings in this present life[c]. For some people are punished by losing what they have. Some are deprived of things. Some suffer from various diseases. Some suffer from every kind of[k] trouble. Some are insulted by unworthy people and suffer in many other undertakings[i].

“For many cannot settle on what to do. They begin many things[d], but nothing succeeds for them. They say that none of their efforts prosper. It does not occur to them[e] that they have done evil; instead, they blame the Lord.”

“When, then, they suffer every kind of affliction, they are handed over to me for good correction and training. Their faith in the Lord[f] grows stronger, and for the rest of their lives they serve him with pure hearts. But if they repent[j], then the evil deeds they did come to mind. Then they glorify God and say that he judges rightly, and that each of them suffered justly for what they had done. From then on, they serve the Lord with pure hearts. They prosper in all they do and receive from the Lord whatever they ask. Then they glorify the Lord because they were handed over to me, and they no longer suffer any of those evils.”

translation:
  text: 'Therefore, seeing them being scourged[g] and harried like this, I was grieved for them, because
    they were being tormented in this way and had no respite at all. I said to the shepherd who was speaking
    with me[a], “Sir, who is this shepherd, so[k] pitiless and harsh, showing no compassion at all for
    these sheep?” He said, “This is the angel of punishment[b]; he is one of the righteous angels, appointed
    over punishment. Therefore he takes over those[h] who have wandered away from God and have gone after
    the desires and deceits of this age, and he punishes them, as they deserve, with dreadful and various
    punishments.”


    “I wished, Sir,” I said, “to know what these various punishments are.” He said, “Listen. The various
    punishments and torments are torments of this present life[c]: for some are punished with losses,
    some with deprivations, some with various sicknesses, some with every kind of[k] disorder; some are
    insulted by the unworthy, and suffer in many other undertakings[i]. For many, being unsettled in their
    plans, take on many projects[d], and nothing at all advances for them. They say of themselves that
    they do not prosper in their undertakings, and it does not rise up into their heart[e] that they have
    done evil, but they blame the Lord.


    “When, then, they are pressed by every affliction, then they are handed over to me for good discipline,
    and they are strengthened in faith in the Lord[f]; and the rest of the days of their life they serve
    the Lord with a pure heart. And if they repent[j], then the evil works that they did rise up into
    their heart; and then they glorify God, saying that he is a righteous judge and that each one suffered
    justly according to his deeds. Thereafter they serve the Lord with a pure heart, and they prosper
    in every work of theirs, receiving from the Lord whatever they ask for; and then they glorify the
    Lord because they were handed over to me, and they no longer suffer any of the evils.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    text: The 'shepherd who was speaking with me' is the angelic guide figure in Hermas, often identified
      with the Shepherd/Angel of repentance.
    reason: cultural_note
  - marker: b
    text: '''Angel of punishment'' could also be rendered ''angel of retribution.'' The Greek τιμωρία
      denotes punitive justice.'
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: c
    text: '''Torments of this present life'' clarifies that βιωτικαί refers to temporal, not eschatological,
      afflictions.'
    reason: cultural_note
  - marker: d
    text: '''Take on many projects'' could also be ''impose many burdens on themselves'' or ''attempt
      many things.'''
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: e
    text: '''It does not rise up into their heart'' is a Semitic-style idiom for ''it does not occur to
      them'' or ''they do not realize.'''
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: f
    text: '''Strengthened in faith in the Lord'' could also be taken as ''strengthened in the Lord’s faithfulness.''
      The context favors faith directed toward the Lord.'
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: g
    text: 'Previous rendering: ''Seeing them being scourged''. The current rendering also expresses οὖν,
      ''therefore.'''
    reason: previous_rendering
  - marker: h
    text: 'Previous rendering: ''He takes over those''. The current rendering also expresses οὖν, ''therefore.'''
    reason: previous_rendering
  - marker: i
    text: 'Previous rendering: ''and they suffer many other such things''. The current ''undertakings''
      preserves πράξεσι and its connection with the following discussion of their activities.'
    reason: previous_rendering
  - marker: j
    text: Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted
      to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while
      preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance;
      do not impose a different tradition on it.
    reason: lexical_alternative

- source_word: μαστιγούμενα
  chosen: scourged
  alternatives:
  - flogged
  - whipped
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Maintains strong punitive imagery of being beaten with lashes; fits the scene of harsh correction.
- source_word: ταλαιπωρούμενα
  chosen: harried
  alternatives:
  - made miserable
  - ill-treated
  - afflicted
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Conveys ongoing wretched hardship; paired with scourged to avoid redundancy.
- source_word: ἐβασανίζοντο / βάσανοι
  chosen: tormented / torments
  alternatives:
  - tortured
  - distresses
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Βάσανος/βασανίζω commonly denote severe testing/torment; 'torment' keeps intensity without
    anachronism.
- source_word: ἀνοχή
  chosen: respite
  alternatives:
  - patience
  - tolerance
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Reconsideration of prior lexical decision: in this clause, ἀνοχή denotes respite from the
    ongoing torment, not deficient endurance or staying power in the sufferers. The current text renders
    ''no respite at all.'''
- source_word: Κύριε (vocative to the shepherd)
  chosen: Sir
  alternatives:
  - Lord
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Here it is respectful address to an angelic guide, not a title for God; 'Sir' avoids theological
    confusion.
- source_word: ἄσπλαγχνος
  chosen: pitiless
  alternatives:
  - without compassion
  - heartless
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Idiomatic and strong; captures lack of compassion inherent in the term.
- source_word: πικρός
  chosen: harsh
  alternatives:
  - bitter
  - severe
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: In moral description of a person, 'harsh' is natural English and preserves severity.
- source_word: ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς τιμωρίας
  chosen: the angel of punishment
  alternatives:
  - angel of retribution
  - avenging angel
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: τιμωρία is punitive justice; 'punishment' is the most transparent and least interpretive
    rendering.
- source_word: ἐκ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν δικαίων
  chosen: one of the righteous angels
  alternatives:
  - from the just angels
  - one of the just angels
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: δίκαιος here denotes moral righteousness; 'righteous angels' is clear and idiomatic.
- source_word: κείμενος ἐπὶ τῆς τιμωρίας
  chosen: appointed over punishment
  alternatives:
  - set over punishment
  - assigned to punishment
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: κείμαι + ἐπί often means to be appointed/established over something.
- source_word: ἀποπλανηθέντας
  chosen: those who have wandered away
  alternatives:
  - those led astray
  - those who strayed
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Keeps the wandering/straying imagery common to shepherding contexts.
- source_word: ἐπιθυμίαις καὶ ἀπάταις τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου
  chosen: the desires and deceits of this age
  alternatives:
  - lusts and deceptions of this age
  - desires and illusions of this age
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Balances literalness and readability; 'this age' preserves the temporal worldview of Hermas.
- source_word: δειναῖς καὶ ποικίλαις (τιμωρίαις)
  chosen: dreadful and various
  alternatives:
  - grievous and manifold
  - terrible and many
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: '''Dreadful'' captures the alarming force of δεινός; ''various'' is standard for ποικίλος.'
- source_word: βιωτικαί (βάσανοι)
  chosen: of this present life
  alternatives:
  - worldly
  - temporal
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Clarifies that the torments are not eschatological but belong to life here and now.
- source_word: ζημίαις
  chosen: losses
  alternatives:
  - penalties
  - forfeitures
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: In context of life-punishments, 'losses' (financial/material) fits well.
- source_word: ὑστερήσεσιν
  chosen: deprivations
  alternatives:
  - lack
  - shortages
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Plural abstract captures various forms of lacking; stronger than simple 'lack'.
- source_word: ἀσθενείαις
  chosen: sicknesses
  alternatives:
  - illnesses
  - weaknesses
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: '''Sicknesses'' fits concrete life-punishments and avoids ambiguity of ''weaknesses''.'
- source_word: ἀκαταστασία
  chosen: disorder
  alternatives:
  - turmoil
  - instability
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: General term for upheaval/disruption; 'disorder' covers societal and personal chaos.
- source_word: ὑβριζόμενοι ὑπὸ ἀναξίων
  chosen: insulted by the unworthy
  alternatives:
  - abused by those unworthy
  - treated with insolence by the unworthy
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: ὑβρίζω often implies insolent abuse; 'insulted' is concise and retains the social humiliation.
- source_word: ἀκαταστατοῦντες ταῖς βουλαῖς
  chosen: being unsettled in their plans
  alternatives:
  - unstable in their schemes
  - in turmoil with their plans
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Reflects inner disorder that yields poor outcomes; keeps 'plans' for βουλαί.
- source_word: ἐπιβάλλονται πολλά
  chosen: take on many projects
  alternatives:
  - impose many burdens on themselves
  - attempt many things
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Idiomatic English capturing self-initiated overextension; 'projects' renders implicit objects
    of action.
- source_word: προχωρεῖ
  chosen: advances
  alternatives:
  - makes progress
  - goes forward
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: '''Advance'' succinctly expresses success/progress of endeavors.'
- source_word: εὐοδοῦσθαι
  chosen: prosper
  alternatives:
  - succeed
  - be made to prosper
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Standard rendering for flourishing of undertakings; repeated later for consistency.
- source_word: οὐκ ἀναβαίνει ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν
  chosen: does not rise up into their heart
  alternatives:
  - does not come into their heart
  - does not occur to them
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Retains Semitic-style idiom while understandable; footnote offers smoother alternative.
- source_word: αἰτιῶνται τὸν Κύριον
  chosen: they blame the Lord
  alternatives:
  - they accuse the Lord
  - they fault the Lord
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: αἰτιάομαι + acc. = blame; 'blame' is clear and idiomatic.
- source_word: παραδίδονται (ἐμοί)
  chosen: are handed over (to me)
  alternatives:
  - are delivered over
  - are entrusted to me
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Paradosis language of transfer to an authority; 'handed over' fits judicial/disciplinary

- source_word: ἀγαθὴ παιδεία
  chosen: good discipline
  alternatives:
  - beneficial discipline

  lexicon: BDAG

- source_word: ἰσχυροποιοῦνται
  chosen: are strengthened
  alternatives:
  - are made strong
  - are fortified
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Passive of making strong; 'strengthened' is concise and natural.
- source_word: ἡ πίστις τοῦ Κυρίου
  chosen: faith in the Lord
  alternatives:
  - the Lord’s faithfulness
  - the faith of the Lord
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Genitive best taken as objective: their faith directed to the Lord; see theological note.'

  chosen: serve the Lord
  alternatives:
  - are enslaved to the Lord

  lexicon: BDAG

translation:
  text: 'So when I saw them being whipped[g] and made to suffer like this, I was grieved for them. They
    were being tormented without any relief. I asked the shepherd who was speaking with me[a], “Sir, who
    is this shepherd? He is so[k] pitiless and harsh and shows these sheep no mercy.”


    He answered, “This is the angel of punishment[b]. He is one of the righteous angels. He is appointed
    to oversee punishment. So he takes charge of those[h] who have wandered away from God and followed
    the desires and deceptions of this age. He punishes them as they deserve with many kinds of terrible
    punishments.”


    “Sir,” I said, “I want to know what these different punishments are.”


    He replied, “Listen. These different punishments and torments are sufferings in this present life[c].
    For some people are punished by losing what they have. Some are deprived of things. Some suffer from
    various diseases. Some suffer from every kind of[k] trouble. Some are insulted by unworthy people
    and suffer in many other undertakings[i].


    “For many cannot settle on what to do. They begin many things[d], but nothing succeeds for them. They
    say that none of their efforts prosper. It does not occur to them[e] that they have done evil; instead,
    they blame the Lord.”


    “When, then, they suffer every kind of affliction, they are handed over to me for good correction
    and training. Their faith in the Lord[f] grows stronger, and for the rest of their lives they serve
    him with pure hearts. But if they repent[j], then the evil deeds they did come to mind. Then they
    glorify God and say that he judges rightly, and that each of them suffered justly for what they had
    done. From then on, they serve the Lord with pure hearts. They prosper in all they do and receive
    from the Lord whatever they ask. Then they glorify the Lord because they were handed over to me, and
    they no longer suffer any of those evils.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    text: The 'shepherd who was speaking with me' is the angelic guide figure in Hermas, often identified
      with the Shepherd/Angel of repentance.
    reason: cultural_note
  - marker: b
    text: '''Angel of punishment'' could also be rendered ''angel of retribution.'' The Greek τιμωρία
      denotes punitive justice.'
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: c
    text: '''Sufferings in this present life'' expresses βιωτικαί: these afflictions belong to present
      life, not the last judgment.'
    reason: cultural_note
  - marker: d
    text: '''Begin many things'' renders ἐπιβάλλονται πολλά. Alternatives include ''take on many projects''
      and ''attempt many things.'''
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: e
    text: '''It does not occur to them'' expresses the Greek heart idiom, rendered in the standard edition
      as ''it does not rise up into their heart.'' It means that they do not realize what they have done.'
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: f
    text: '''Their faith in the Lord grows stronger'' takes the Greek as faith directed toward the Lord.
      The phrase could also be understood as being strengthened in the Lord’s faithfulness.'
    reason: lexical_alternative
  - marker: g
    text: 'Previous standard-edition rendering: ''Seeing them being scourged''. This edition uses ''whipped''
      and also expresses οὖν with ''So.'''
    reason: previous_rendering
  - marker: h
    text: 'Previous standard-edition rendering: ''He takes over those''. This edition uses ''takes charge
      of'' and also expresses οὖν with ''So.'''
    reason: previous_rendering
  - marker: i
    text: 'Previous standard-edition rendering: ''and they suffer many other such things''. ''Undertakings''
      means activities or things they attempt; it preserves πράξεσι and its connection with the following
      discussion.'
    reason: previous_rendering
  - marker: j
    text: Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted
      to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while
      preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance;
      do not impose a different tradition on it.
    reason: lexical_alternative

    text: '''So'' in ''so pitiless'' and ''every kind of'' render οὕτως and πάσῃ, respectively, which
      appear in square brackets in the supplied working source. This reports their editorially marked
      status in that source, not independent manuscript verification.'
    reason: source_status

- source_word: μαστιγούμενα
  chosen: whipped
  alternatives:
  - flogged
  - whipped
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Maintains strong punitive imagery of being beaten with lashes; fits the scene of harsh correction.
- source_word: ταλαιπωρούμενα
  chosen: made to suffer
  alternatives:
  - made miserable
  - ill-treated
  - afflicted
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''made to suffer'' expresses the hardship of ταλαιπωρούμενα
    alongside ''whipped.'' The standard edition uses ''harried.'''
- source_word: ἐβασανίζοντο / βάσανοι
  chosen: tormented / torments / sufferings
  alternatives:
  - tortured
  - distresses
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Βάσανος/βασανίζω commonly denote severe testing/torment; 'torment' keeps intensity without
    anachronism.
- source_word: ἀνοχή
  chosen: relief
  alternatives:
  - patience
  - tolerance
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Reconsideration of prior lexical decision: ἀνοχή here denotes respite from ongoing torment,
    not deficient staying power. This edition simplifies ''respite'' to ''relief.'''
- source_word: Κύριε (vocative to the shepherd)
  chosen: Sir
  alternatives:
  - Lord
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Here it is respectful address to an angelic guide, not a title for God; 'Sir' avoids theological
    confusion.
- source_word: ἄσπλαγχνος
  chosen: pitiless
  alternatives:
  - without compassion
  - heartless
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: Idiomatic and strong; captures lack of compassion inherent in the term.
- source_word: πικρός
  chosen: harsh
  alternatives:
  - bitter
  - severe
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: In moral description of a person, 'harsh' is natural English and preserves severity.
- source_word: ὁ ἄγγελος τῆς τιμωρίας
  chosen: the angel of punishment
  alternatives:
  - angel of retribution
  - avenging angel
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: τιμωρία is punitive justice; 'punishment' is the most transparent and least interpretive
    rendering.
- source_word: ἐκ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν δικαίων
  chosen: one of the righteous angels
  alternatives:
  - from the just angels
  - one of the just angels
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: δίκαιος here denotes moral righteousness; 'righteous angels' is clear and idiomatic.
- source_word: κείμενος ἐπὶ τῆς τιμωρίας
  chosen: appointed to oversee punishment
  alternatives:
  - set over punishment
  - assigned to punishment
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: κείμαι + ἐπί often means to be appointed/established over something.
- source_word: ἀποπλανηθέντας
  chosen: those who have wandered away
  alternatives:
  - those led astray
  - those who strayed
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Keeps the wandering/straying imagery common to shepherding contexts.
- source_word: ἐπιθυμίαις καὶ ἀπάταις τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου
  chosen: the desires and deceptions of this age
  alternatives:
  - lusts and deceptions of this age
  - desires and illusions of this age
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Balances literalness and readability; 'this age' preserves the temporal worldview of Hermas.
- source_word: δειναῖς καὶ ποικίλαις (τιμωρίαις)
  chosen: many kinds of terrible
  alternatives:
  - grievous and manifold
  - terrible and many
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''terrible'' preserves the severity of δεινός, and ''many
    kinds of'' expresses the variety denoted by ποικίλος. The standard edition uses ''dreadful and various.'''
- source_word: βιωτικαί (βάσανοι)
  chosen: in this present life
  alternatives:
  - worldly
  - temporal
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Clarifies that the torments are not eschatological but belong to life here and now.
- source_word: ζημίαις
  chosen: losing what they have
  alternatives:
  - penalties
  - forfeitures
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: In context of life-punishments, 'losses' (financial/material) fits well.
- source_word: ὑστερήσεσιν
  chosen: deprived of things
  alternatives:
  - lack
  - shortages
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''deprived of things'' expresses the lack or deprivation
    denoted by ὑστερήσεσιν without specifying possessions or needs not named in the clause.'
- source_word: ἀσθενείαις
  chosen: diseases
  alternatives:
  - illnesses
  - weaknesses
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''diseases'' expresses bodily illness among these present-life
    punishments. The standard edition uses ''sicknesses''; ''weaknesses'' remains an alternative gloss.'
- source_word: ἀκαταστασία
  chosen: trouble
  alternatives:
  - turmoil
  - instability
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''trouble'' uses a general term for the disruption or instability
    denoted by ἀκαταστασία. The standard edition uses ''disorder.'''
- source_word: ὑβριζόμενοι ὑπὸ ἀναξίων
  chosen: insulted by unworthy people
  alternatives:
  - abused by those unworthy
  - treated with insolence by the unworthy
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: ὑβρίζω often implies insolent abuse; 'insulted' is concise and retains the social humiliation.
- source_word: ἀκαταστατοῦντες ταῖς βουλαῖς
  chosen: cannot settle on what to do
  alternatives:
  - unstable in their schemes
  - in turmoil with their plans
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''cannot settle on what to do'' expresses being unsettled
    in their plans, ἀκαταστατοῦντες ταῖς βουλαῖς. It does not retain ''plans'' as an explicit noun.'
- source_word: ἐπιβάλλονται πολλά
  chosen: begin many things
  alternatives:
  - impose many burdens on themselves
  - attempt many things
  lexicon: LSJ
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''begin many things'' expresses undertaking multiple activities.
    The standard edition uses ''take on many projects''; this wording does not independently assert that
    the activities exceed their capacity.'
- source_word: προχωρεῖ
  chosen: succeeds
  alternatives:
  - makes progress
  - goes forward
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''succeeds'' expresses the lack of progress or success
    in their activities denoted by οὐδὲν…προχωρεῖ. The standard edition uses ''advances.'''
- source_word: εὐοδοῦσθαι
  chosen: prosper
  alternatives:
  - succeed
  - be made to prosper
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Standard rendering for flourishing of undertakings; repeated later for consistency.
- source_word: οὐκ ἀναβαίνει ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν
  chosen: does not occur to them
  alternatives:
  - does not come into their heart
  - does not occur to them
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''does not occur to them'' states the meaning of the Greek
    heart idiom. The note preserves the standard edition''s more literal ''does not rise up into their
    heart.'''
- source_word: αἰτιῶνται τὸν Κύριον
  chosen: they blame the Lord
  alternatives:
  - they accuse the Lord
  - they fault the Lord
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: αἰτιάομαι + acc. = blame; 'blame' is clear and idiomatic.
- source_word: παραδίδονται (ἐμοί)
  chosen: are handed over (to me)
  alternatives:
  - are delivered over
  - are entrusted to me
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: Paradosis language of transfer to an authority; 'handed over' fits judicial/disciplinary
    context.
- source_word: ἀγαθὴ παιδεία
  chosen: good correction and training
  alternatives:
  - beneficial discipline
  - wholesome training
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''correction and training'' explains παιδεία, and ''good''
    preserves ἀγαθή. The standard edition uses ''good discipline.'''
- source_word: ἰσχυροποιοῦνται
  chosen: grows stronger
  alternatives:
  - are made strong
  - are fortified
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''their faith…grows stronger'' paraphrases their being
    strengthened in faith. The Greek verb is passive; this English formulation does not identify an additional
    agent or remove the linked faith alternative in the note.'
- source_word: ἡ πίστις τοῦ Κυρίου
  chosen: faith in the Lord
  alternatives:
  - the Lord’s faithfulness
  - the faith of the Lord
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Genitive best taken as objective: their faith directed to the Lord; see theological note.'
- source_word: δουλεύουσι τῷ Κυρίῳ
  chosen: serve the Lord
  alternatives:
  - are enslaved to the Lord
  - are in service to the Lord
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Reconsideration of prior lexical rationale: ''serve'' expresses devoted obedience to the
    Lord here. δουλεύουσι retains a slave-service background; the reader wording does not deny that background
    or specify a particular historical institution of slavery.'
- source_word: μετανοήσωσι
  chosen: repent
  alternatives:
  - reorient
  - repent
  - change their mind
  - turn back
  lexicon: Recorded source/witness and contextual review; see docs/REPENTANCE_REASSESSMENT_2026-10-13.md
  rationale: Use repentance for moral change while preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness,
    conduct and the angel of repentance; do not impose a different tradition on it. Contextual editorial
    assessment, not independent scholarly certification.
  doctrine_reference: 'DOCTRINE.md: Repentance terminology (2026-10-13)'
- source_word: ἀναβαίνει ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν
  chosen: come to mind
  alternatives:
  - come into their heart
  - occur to them
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''come to mind'' expresses realization or recollection
    of the evil deeds they did. The standard edition retains the heart imagery. The preceding ''if'' preserves
    the condition ἐὰν μετανοήσωσι.'
- source_word: δίκαιος κριτής
  chosen: he judges rightly
  alternatives:
  - just judge
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''he judges rightly'' expresses God as a righteous judge
    through a verb and adverb. The standard edition retains the noun phrase ''righteous judge.'''
- source_word: δικαίως ἔπαθον
  chosen: suffered justly
  alternatives:
  - received what was just
  - were punished justly
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: ἔπαθον is broad ('suffered/experienced'); 'suffered justly' matches context without over-specifying

- source_word: εὐοδοῦνται ἐν πάσῃ πράξει
  chosen: prosper in all they do
  alternatives:
  - succeed in every undertaking
  - are made to prosper in all they do
  lexicon: BDAG
  rationale: 'Edition-specific simplification: ''all they do'' expresses πάσῃ πράξει without the noun

    rather than weakened.'

base_translation:
  text: 'Therefore, seeing them being scourged[g] and harried like this, I was grieved for them, because
    they were being tormented in this way and had no respite at all. I said to the shepherd who was speaking
    with me[a], “Sir, who is this shepherd, so[k] pitiless and harsh, showing no compassion at all for
    these sheep?” He said, “This is the angel of punishment[b]; he is one of the righteous angels, appointed
    over punishment. Therefore he takes over those[h] who have wandered away from God and have gone after
    the desires and deceits of this age, and he punishes them, as they deserve, with dreadful and various
    punishments.”


    “I wished, Sir,” I said, “to know what these various punishments are.” He said, “Listen. The various
    punishments and torments are torments of this present life[c]: for some are punished with losses,
    some with deprivations, some with various sicknesses, some with every kind of[k] disorder; some are
    insulted by the unworthy, and suffer in many other undertakings[i]. For many, being unsettled in their
    plans, take on many projects[d], and nothing at all advances for them. They say of themselves that
    they do not prosper in their undertakings, and it does not rise up into their heart[e] that they have
    done evil, but they blame the Lord.


    “When, then, they are pressed by every affliction, then they are handed over to me for good discipline,
    and they are strengthened in faith in the Lord[f]; and the rest of the days of their life they serve
    the Lord with a pure heart. And if they repent[j], then the evil works that they did rise up into
    their heart; and then they glorify God, saying that he is a righteous judge and that each one suffered
    justly according to his deeds. Thereafter they serve the Lord with a pure heart, and they prosper
    in every work of theirs, receiving from the Lord whatever they ask for; and then they glorify the
    Lord because they were handed over to me, and they no longer suffer any of the evils.”'
